// purpose: @debuggen/panel-schema - the compiler project for the monorepo typecheck gate. `pnpm typecheck` (= `pnpm demo:generate && tsc -b`) builds the root solution file, whose `references` list this project after packages/shared and packages/telemetry: panel-schema sits on the schema layer of the acyclic package graph (AAP 0.2.2) and depends on exactly those two workspaces, so `references` below has exactly those two entries in that order and `tsc -b` builds shared -> telemetry -> panel-schema. The sibling `tsup.config.ts` points at this same file with `tsconfig: "./tsconfig.json"`, so the bundle and the gate type-check the package under one identical configuration.
// package: What this package is: the panel specification DSL - the authoring schema a model may produce (input.ts), the deterministic normaliser (normalize.ts), the internal PanelSpec with its evidence and data-query types (spec.ts, summary.ts, nodes/{query,layout,viz}.ts), the node catalog (catalog.ts) and the syntactic and semantic validators (validate.ts, semantic.ts, json-schema.ts). It is pure Zod schema and pure data: no React, no DOM, no Node builtins, no I/O.
// inherited: Everything not stated below is inherited from tsconfig.base.json and must stay that way - in particular `strict`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `verbatimModuleSyntax`, `isolatedModules`, `noImplicitOverride`, `noImplicitReturns`, `noFallthroughCasesInSwitch`, `noUnusedLocals`, `noUnusedParameters`, `forceConsistentCasingInFileNames`, `target`/`lib` ES2023 and the declaration-emit settings (`declaration`, `declarationMap`, `sourceMap`, `emitDeclarationOnly`, `incremental`). No strictness flag is relaxed here, and no compiler version or compiler package is declared: TypeScript 6.0.3 is pinned once, in the root manifest (AAP 0.3.1). `noEmit` must never be added: TypeScript 6.0.3 rejects a referenced project that disables emit with TS6310 and the whole gate fails.
// format: Strict JSON, like tsconfig.base.json, the root tsconfig.json and every other tsconfig in this repository: both a JSONC-aware reader (`ts.readConfigFile`) and a bare `JSON.parse` can read it, so no consumer has to know which one to reach for. tsc, ESLint, Vitest, tsup and Prettier would all accept comments in a tsconfig file, but the rationale is recorded in the `"// …"` string keys of this object instead so that every reader gets it. TypeScript ignores unknown TOP-LEVEL keys, which is what makes the convention safe; a `"// …"` key inside `compilerOptions` is a hard error instead (TS5023, "Unknown compiler option"), so every note about a single option lives up here under a `"// compilerOptions.<option>"` key and never beside the option itself.
// compilerOptions.composite: Already true in the base; restated because the root solution file references this project and a non-composite reference fails `tsc -b` outright (TS6306). Keeping it local means a future edit to the base cannot silently break the gate at this project.
// compilerOptions.module: The base defaults to "ESNext" + "bundler" for the bundled/web workspaces and instructs Node-targeted projects to override with NodeNext (AAP 0.3.4). This package is one of them: package.json declares `"type": "module"` and dist/index.js is imported directly by the Node process apps/local-service (src/panels/{generate,validate,fallback}.ts, src/pipeline/stages/generate-panel.ts) as well as by the bundled surfaces (the DevTools panel through @debuggen/panel-renderer, and @debuggen/protocol's panel message). NodeNext output is consumable by Node *and* by every bundler in the repo; the reverse is not true, so the stricter flavour is the correct default - and it matches the choice both sibling schema packages made (packages/shared, packages/telemetry). CONSEQUENCE FOR EVERY SOURCE FILE IN src/** - the single most common build break in this workspace: relative specifiers must carry an explicit ".js" extension even though the files on disk are ".ts", and directory specifiers must name the file: `import { factSchema } from "./summary.js";`, `import { dataQuerySchema } from "./nodes/query.js";`, `export * from "./spec.js";`. Extensionless relative imports are a compile error here by design (TS2835), because they would break the real Node consumer of dist/index.js. Package specifiers are written WITHOUT an extension - `zod`, `@debuggen/shared`, `@debuggen/telemetry` - and resolve through the pnpm workspace symlink and each package's `exports` map. tsup/esbuild resolve a "./x.js" specifier from a TypeScript importer back to "./x.ts", so the emitted bundle is unaffected. `verbatimModuleSyntax` is inherited, so a specifier imported only for its types must say `import type` / `export type`. Both forms occur in this package and both must compile: semantic.ts consumes `CaptureSummary` purely as a type (`import type { CaptureSummary } from "@debuggen/telemetry"`), while catalog.ts and nodes/query.ts need the RUNTIME values that package owns - the telemetry kind list and kind groups, the kind-specific attribute key catalogs and `METRIC_IDS` - and sourceLocationSchema is imported as a runtime value from `@debuggen/shared`.
// compilerOptions.rootDir: Per-workspace (the base deliberately leaves it unset), so the declaration tree under .tsbuild/ mirrors src/ exactly: src/index.ts -> .tsbuild/index.d.ts and src/nodes/query.ts -> .tsbuild/nodes/query.d.ts, matching the path the package.json `exports` map advertises under dist/. It also pins the program's boundary: nothing outside src/ may be an input.
// compilerOptions.outDir: NOT overridden: "outDir" / "declarationDir" / "tsBuildInfoFile". The base anchors all three per project with `${configDir}`, which resolves to the directory of THIS file and not to the base's own directory, so the declarations and the incremental stamp already land in packages/panel-schema/.tsbuild (ignored by .gitignore and .prettierignore). Restating a bare relative "outDir": ".tsbuild" here would resolve to the same place and is therefore redundant. tsc must never write into packages/panel-schema/dist: that directory belongs to tsup and holds the artefacts the `exports` map points at.
// compilerOptions.lib: NOT overridden. The base's ES2023-only set is exactly right - this package must never touch a browser API. It is consumed by the DevTools panel, but only as pure schema and data, so adding "DOM" would legitimise `window`/`document` in a module that also runs inside the local service.
// compilerOptions.types: NOT set. The base leaves it unset so one workspace's ambient globals cannot bleed into another, and this package needs none: the library subtree is environment-neutral (the sibling tsup.config.ts sets `platform: "neutral"` so an accidental Node builtin fails the build rather than shipping a barrel that breaks browser consumers), and the colocated tests use no Node builtin - they build their fixtures as literals and validate them with the schemas under test. Adding "node" here would make `process`, `Buffer` and `require` ambient across the whole library and let exactly that mistake compile. If a future test genuinely needs a builtin, add "types": ["node"] and keep the `node:*` import inside the test file.
// compilerOptions.jsx: NOT set. The base's inherited "react-jsx" is inert because `include` below admits no .tsx file, and none exists: this package contains no React (packages/telemetry needs it only for its src/browser/react.test.tsx).
// compilerOptions.paths: NOT set: "paths" / "baseUrl". The two workspace dependencies resolve through their `exports` maps plus the project references below, exactly as the runtime and the bundlers resolve them (AAP 0.2.2). Aliasing to source would hide a broken `exports` map and let the acyclic layering be violated without anything failing.
// compilerOptions.noEmit: NOT set, and no strictness flag is relaxed on top of the base.
// include: src/** only, and .ts only. This covers the library modules (index.ts, input.ts, normalize.ts, spec.ts, summary.ts, catalog.ts, validate.ts, semantic.ts, json-schema.ts, nodes/{query,layout,viz}.ts) and the colocated `*.test.ts` suites (input, normalize, validate, semantic, catalog), which are deliberately part of the program so the typecheck gate covers them: `strict`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `noUnusedLocals` and `noUnusedParameters` apply to tests exactly as they do to sources. Tests import `{ describe, it, expect }` from "vitest" explicitly rather than relying on globals, so no "vitest/globals" entry is needed in `types`. Until the first src file lands, `tsc -b` on this project answers TS18003 ("No inputs were found in config file") - expected on an empty subtree, not a configuration fault.
// exclude: Replaces the base's inherited list rather than merging with it, so the build output directories are named again here; resolved relative to this directory, meaning packages/panel-schema/{dist,node_modules,.tsbuild}. `include` already restricts the input set to src/**, which leaves dist/ (tsup output) and .tsbuild/ (declaration output) outside the program; these entries document that intent and keep it true if `include` is ever widened. Note what `exclude` does NOT do: it filters the `include` globs only, so a file reached by an import still joins the program - `rootDir` above is what rejects one from outside src/ (TS6059).
// references: The ONLY project references, foundational-first to match the root solution's ordering. @debuggen/panel-schema depends on @debuggen/shared (the single `SourceLocation` definition, reused rather than restated) and on @debuggen/telemetry (the telemetry event kinds, the attribute-key catalogs and the fixed metric-id set owned by its aggregate/summary.ts, likewise referenced rather than restated), and on no other workspace - exactly the edges AAP 0.2.2 gives this package and exactly its package.json `dependencies`. What the references do, precisely: they order the build, so `tsc -b` on this project (or on the root solution) builds packages/shared and then packages/telemetry before this project and reports errors in dependency order. They are NOT what resolves the two specifiers: each package's `exports` map points at its tsup output (dist/index.d.ts), which lies outside the `${configDir}/.tsbuild` declaration directory `tsc -b` writes, so no output-to-source redirect applies. That is deliberate - it type-checks this package against the very declarations its consumers import (AAP 0.2.2) - and it holds on every built tree. Only where a dependency's dist/ does not exist yet (a fresh clone) does the second entry of its `types` fallback array - the package's src/ entry - apply, and `tsc -b` redirects that to the referenced project's own `.tsbuild` declarations; that is what lets `pnpm typecheck` stand alone without `pnpm build` (AAP 0.8.5), as tests/e2e/clean-clone.spec.ts proves on a fresh copy of the tree. Never add ../protocol or ../panel-renderer, nor any app: both sit ABOVE this package in the layering (protocol embeds the panel spec in its panel.generated message; panel-renderer keys its component registry by this package's node catalog). A reference in either direction is the project-reference cycle that `tsc -b` rejects, and importing them from here is independently forbidden by the `no-restricted-imports` rules in the root eslint.config.js.
